{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Most gains in working conditions for home care workers in the past decade have come through state and county governments negotiating collective bargaining agreements with unions.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Collective bargaining agreements require private agencies that hire home care workers to employ them according to standards of a union contract negotiated with the government, which then contracts with these private agencies.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"It is particularly justifiable that agencies employ workers according to union contract standards given that the agencies receive public funding to pay these workers.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Union contracts have lifted hundreds of thousands of low-wage workers out of poverty.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Union contracts have compelled agencies employing workers to grant employees greater break and vacation time and more humane working conditions.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Union contracts have led to less turnover and higher quality care for the clients for whom these workers care.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Court’s decision threatens the gains made by union contracts.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
